assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: pH
items.clue: The negative logarithm to base 10 of the hydrogen ion concentration.

items.label: Strong acid
items.clue: A proton donor that is fully ionized in aqueous solution, such as HCl.

items.label: Neutralization
items.clue: The reaction of an acid with a base, such as HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l).

items.label: Salt
items.clue: Ionic compound formed, usually together with water, when an acid reacts with a base.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid is diluted with distilled water to a total volume of 250 cm³. What is the pH of the diluted solution?
questions.explanation: Amount of HCl = 0.100 mol dm⁻³ × 0.0250 dm³ = 2.50 × 10⁻³ mol. In 0.250 dm³, [H⁺] = 1.00 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³, so pH = −log₁₀(1.00 × 10⁻²) = 2.00. A 10-fold dilution raises the pH by 1 unit.

questions.stem: At 298 K, solution P has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ and solution Q has [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Kw = 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K. How does [OH⁻] in P compare with [OH⁻] in Q?

options.text: It is 100 times larger in P than in Q.
It is the same, as acid has no effect on [OH⁻].
Neither contains OH⁻ ions, as both are acidic.
It is 100 times smaller in P than in Q.

questions.explanation: [OH⁻] = Kw/[H⁺]. P: 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 1.0 × 10⁻³ = 1.0 × 10⁻¹¹ mol dm⁻³; Q: 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ / 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁹ mol dm⁻³. P has 100 times the [H⁺] of Q, so it has 1/100 of the [OH⁻].

questions.stem: A solution of nitric acid, HNO₃(aq), has a concentration of 0.0010 mol dm⁻³. Which statement about this solution is correct?

options.text: It is a weak acid, as its concentration is low.
It contains mainly HNO₃ molecules with a few ions.
It is a dilute solution of an acid that is fully ionized.
It is neutral, as this much water neutralizes the acid.

questions.explanation: HNO₃ is a strong acid, so it is fully ionized at this concentration: HNO₃ → H⁺ + NO₃⁻, and [H⁺] = 0.0010 mol dm⁻³. At 0.0010 mol dm⁻³ the solution is dilute. Strength (extent of ionization) and concentration are independent.

questions.stem: Which statement about measuring the pH of an aqueous solution is correct?

options.text: Universal indicator is as precise as a pH meter.
A new pH meter reads accurately before it is calibrated.
A calibrated pH meter can give the pH to about 0.01 unit.
A reading of 7.00 shows a neutral solution at any temperature.

questions.explanation: A pH meter (probe), calibrated with buffer solutions of known pH, gives a numerical reading, typically to 0.01 pH unit. Universal indicator only estimates pH, usually to the nearest whole unit.

questions.stem: A student's data show that an aqueous solution at 323 K has [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 2.34 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³, so its pH is 6.63. Which statement about this solution is correct?

options.text: It is neutral, as its [H⁺] and [OH⁻] are equal.
It is acidic, as its pH is lower than 7.00.
It is acidic, as it contains H⁺(aq) ions.
Both acidic and basic: each ion exceeds 1.0 × 10⁻⁷.

questions.explanation: A solution is neutral when [H⁺] = [OH⁻], at any temperature. pH 7.00 marks neutrality only at 298 K; at 323 K a neutral solution has a lower pH because water is more ionized.

questions.stem:
Hydrogen chloride reacts with water:
HCl(aq) + H₂O(l) → H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
The position of this equilibrium lies so far to the right that the reaction is effectively complete. Which statement about this reaction is correct?

options.text: Cl⁻ is the acid, since HCl forms it.
Cl⁻ is a weaker base than H₂O.
H₃O⁺ is a stronger acid than HCl.
H₂O is the acid, as it gains a proton.

questions.explanation: Acid–base equilibria lie on the side of the weaker acid and weaker base. The products, H₃O⁺ and Cl⁻, are favoured, so Cl⁻ is a weaker base than H₂O (and H₃O⁺ a weaker acid than HCl).

questions.stem: 10.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid of pH 1.70 is diluted with distilled water to a total volume of 1.00 dm³ at 298 K. What is [H⁺] in the diluted solution?

options.text: 0.00020 mol dm⁻³
0.020 mol dm⁻³
0.50 mol dm⁻³
0.0018 mol dm⁻³

questions.explanation: [H⁺] = 10⁻¹·⁷⁰ = 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ in the original acid. Amount of H⁺ = 0.0200 × 0.0100 dm³ = 2.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol, in 1.00 dm³, so [H⁺] = 0.00020 mol dm⁻³ (a 100-fold dilution).

questions.stem: Separate 25.0 cm³ samples of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) and 0.100 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COOH(aq) are each titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq). Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both need the same volume of NaOH(aq), as the acid amounts are equal.
The HCl needs more NaOH(aq), as it releases more H⁺ ions in water.
Both acids start at the same pH, as their acid concentrations are equal.
The CH₃COOH starts at the lower pH, as each molecule has four H atoms.

questions.explanation: Both samples contain 2.50 × 10⁻³ mol of a monoprotic acid, so both need 2.50 × 10⁻³ mol of NaOH (25.0 cm³). As OH⁻ removes H⁺, the ethanoic acid equilibrium shifts to the right until all the acid has reacted.

questions.stem: Solution X is 0.0010 mol dm⁻³ KOH(aq). Solution Y is 2.0 mol dm⁻³ NH₃(aq). Which statement is correct?

options.text: NH₃ is the stronger base, as solution Y is more concentrated.
NH₃ is not a base, as its formula contains no OH group.
KOH is the stronger base, as it is fully ionized.
Both are strong bases, as both release OH⁻ ions in water.

questions.explanation: Strength is the extent of ionization, not concentration. KOH, a group 1 hydroxide, is fully ionized even in this dilute solution; NH₃ reacts only partly with water (NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ lies well to the left), even at 2.0 mol dm⁻³.

questions.stem: At 298 K, 0.10 mol dm⁻³ aqueous solutions have these pH values: HCl 1.0; CH₃COOH 2.9; NH₃ 11.1; NaOH 13.0. Which conclusion is supported by these data?

options.text: HCl is only partly ionized in solution, as its pH is 1.0 rather than 0.0.
NH₃ is a strong base, as its solution has a pH well above 7, at 11.1.
NH₃(aq) needs less HCl(aq) than an equal volume of NaOH(aq) does.
CH₃COOH is a weak acid, as its [H⁺] is far below 0.10 mol dm⁻³.

questions.explanation: pH 2.9 means [H⁺] = 10⁻²·⁹ ≈ 1.3 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³, only about 1% of the 0.10 mol dm⁻³ acid. Most of the CH₃COOH is un-ionized, which is what 'weak' means. HCl at the same concentration gives pH 1.0, [H⁺] = 0.10 mol dm⁻³: complete ionization.
